correctness.rationale: The inverse branch on each closed lap is a strict contraction, hence has one fixed point; no interior knot is fixed, and sorting recovers the branch indices. The first point is always 0, and the last is 1 exactly in odd parity. For each interior lap, solving its affine fixed-point equation expresses the next knot as an affine function of the previous one with nonzero slope. Starting at t=b1, the final even lap determines b_(m-1) from p_m=1/(2-b_(m-1)), so it determines t, including m=2. The final odd lap instead gives p_m=1 identically; strict ordering cuts the one-dimensional affine fiber into a nonempty open interval. A knot cannot be in an exact two-cycle since it maps to an endpoint and endpoints are fixed or map to the fixed endpoint 0. Compositions of two inverse branches are contractions; distinct-lap ordered pairs yield interior primitive points, same-lap pairs yield fixed points, and each primitive point has a unique ordered itinerary. Thus the minimum lies in lap 1 with successor in lap 2 by ordering of inverse ranges. With u=b2, the two-branch return gives q=tu/(1+t(u-t)); substituting p2=u/(1+u-t) gives the claimed inversion and positive fiber derivative. The open odd fiber proves sharp necessity; no noise or nonaffine claim is needed. Exact forward evaluations confirmed the two three-lap examples in /workspace/branches/audit_witnesses.py; the proof covers all real strict knot vectors.
